sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Vehayah ekev tishma'un" and its connection to thought, speech, and action, culminating in the revelation of Atzmus.

translations.translation: "And it shall be, because you will hearken... and you will guard and you will do them..."
And the precise point in this is known,
for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos depends on man's choice,
and it should have said "And it shall be, if you will hearken"
[like "If
you walk in My statutes,
and it shall be
if you surely hearken"],
so why does it say "And it shall be, because you will hearken"?
For the meaning of the language is that you will surely hearken.
And the Tzemach Tzedek explains
that "ekev" refers to the time of the heels of Moshiach,
and this is "And it shall be, because you will hearken" —
you will surely hearken,
for the Torah promised that ultimately Israel will repent at the end of their exile, and immediately they will be redeemed.
And he continues in the maamar,
that the three expressions,
"you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"
are thought, speech, and action.
"You will hearken" is thought,
for the essence of hearing is in thought
(and the ear is merely a vessel through which sound enters his thought),
and "you will guard" is speech,
for the essence of guarding is with the mouth, as it is said,
"arranged in all and guarded,"
and "you will do" is action.
And upon this it continues and says,
"And Hashem your G-d will guard for you the covenant and the kindness which He swore..."
Covenant, kindness, and oath are thought, speech, and action
(as explained there at length),
and through "you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"
the service of thought, speech, and action of man,
there are drawn to him the thought, speech, and action from above,
"the covenant and the kindness which He swore."
However,
this matter
(that the thought, speech, and action from above should be drawn to man)
is still insufficient,
for even before the soul's descent below, it was in the most supernal level of this,
the thought above —
"Israel arose in thought,"
and the descent of the soul below is for the sake of an ascent,
so that through its service below it will ascend to a level more elevated than it was before the descent,
even to the level of "And You
guard it within me"
(which is above even the level of "pure"
it is).
And this is what is said, "And He will guard... the covenant and the kindness which He swore...",
that through "because you will hearken," "you will guard," and "you will do,"
the service of thought, speech, and action in the "heel" of the soul, which refers to the soul within the body,
and particularly in the heels of Moshiach
[an addition in the descent,
and consequently,
also in the ascent that comes through the descent],
that through the descent into a body and animal soul
(and particularly in exile),
the service of thought, speech, and action of the soul is with will and desire and in a manner of self-sacrifice
(above comprehension),
through this there will be "And He will guard... the covenant and the kindness which He swore..."
(specifically "guard"),
that the thought, speech, and action from above will have within them the revelation of "And You guard it within me,"
which in general is the matter of
the revelation of the Awtsmoos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the Tzemach Tzedek's interpretation of "ekev" to the Midrash on reward, linking the service of self-sacrifice in the heels of Moshiach to the future revelation of Atzmus.

translations.translation: b)
And behold, the above explanation
(of the Tzemach Tzedek)
regarding "And it shall be, because you will hearken"
(that "ekev" is an expression of end and refers to the end of days)
can be connected with the statement of the Midrash
on the verse,
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them... their reward
(the reward of the mitzvos)
"in the heel" I give to you...
(as it is said)
"And it shall be, because you will hearken."
However, according to the Midrash which speaks of the reward of mitzvos,
the intent of "ekev"
(the end of days)
is for the time after the coming of Moshiach,
and according to the simple understanding of the matter which speaks of the fulfillment of mitzvos
("you will hearken... and you will guard and you will do them"),
the intent of "ekev"
(the end of days)
is for the end of the time of exile,
the heels of Moshiach.
And the connection between the two explanations is,
for the reward of mitzvos that will be "in the heel"
(in the future to come)
is that then there will be the revelation of the Awtsmoos,
as explained in Tanya.
And since this revelation is through the service
(of Torah and mitzvos in a manner)
of self-sacrifice
(as above),
therefore,
through "because you will hearken" according to the Tzemach Tzedek's explanation,
the service in the heels of Moshiach,
when self-sacrifice is greatest,
through this there will be the revelation of the future to come,
"in the heel I give to you."
